clue.text: Putting off engineer undoing jar

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the letters of 'undoing jar' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frustrated mechanic struggling to open a stuck jar keeps postponing the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineer' looks like a noun, the person doing the putting off, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange UNDOING JAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Postponing a meeting until later is suspending or deferring it, a standard synonym.

clue.text: Key language for gastropod

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
argot is the jargon or slang of a particular group

explanation.surface: A linguist names the crucial vocabulary for describing a snail.
explanation.definitionFit: The French dish of edible snails names a creature that is a gastropod mollusc.

clue.text: Travelled along runway to charge bomb

parts.note: a tax is a charge levied by government
IED is an improvised explosive device, a homemade bomb

explanation.surface: An aircraft rolls down the runway, poised to attack with a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Planes move slowly on the ground between gate and runway before take-off, which is the specialised aviation verb here.

clue.text: Baby finally, by daybreak, dropping head to show sign of tiredness

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Baby
dropping its head means the first letter of the word for daybreak is lost

parts.note: dawn is daybreak

explanation.surface: A baby, woken at first light, shows how tired it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening the mouth wide with a deep breath is the body's involuntary signal of sleepiness or boredom.

clue.text: Money covering up steps to produce plague

indicators.note: covering up means the money word wraps round the steps word

parts.note: pence are small British coins, so money
a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence

explanation.surface: Bribes conceal the stages by which a plague was allowed to spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadly epidemic disease, the bubonic kind especially, is called a pestilence or plague.

clue.text: Drink drunk in haste containing boron

indicators.note: containing means the rearranged letters hold the boron symbol inside them
drunk suggests the letters of 'in haste' are reeling about into a new order

parts.note: B is the chemical symbol for boron

explanation.surface: Someone gulps a chemically laced drink too quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' turns IN HASTE into ASINTHE; 'containing' then puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green anise-flavoured spirit, so a drink.

clue.text: Stick around to get love present

parts.note: c. (circa) is the abbreviation for around, meaning approximately
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
present in the sense of here, in attendance

explanation.surface: Advice to a partner: hang about so you can receive a gift of love.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick together is to hold firmly as a unified whole, which is what cohere means.

clue.text: Rising canal reveals God

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea

explanation.surface: The waters of a canal rise to reveal a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the ruler of the Olympian deities in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Criticise German in crumbling paradise

indicators.note: in means the German letter is placed within the rearranged letters
crumbling means the word paradise falls apart and is rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A German visitor finds fault with a paradise that is falling to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbling' turns PARADISE into DISPARAE; 'in' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle or speak slightingly of something is to run it down, a close synonym of criticise.

clue.text: Cracked globe returned by King Edward, initially

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the king's letters sit next to the turned-round globe
returned means the word for globe is turned round

parts.note: an orb is a globe, especially the royal one carried with the sceptre
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of Edward

explanation.surface: King Edward hands back a damaged royal orb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has cracked has fractured or split, i.e. been damaged and now in pieces.

clue.text: Acclaim unlimited rations, following boundless love

indicators.note: following places the trimmed rations after the trimmed love
boundless means the word love loses its outer limits, its first and last letters
unlimited means the word rations is stripped of its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Diners cheer unrestricted food supplies after a period of boundless affection.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing round of applause is enthusiastic public praise, i.e. acclaim.

clue.text: Muscles in short time before additional message

parts.note: a trice is a moment, as in 'in a trice'
PS is a postscript, the message added after a letter's signature

explanation.surface: A quick note about muscles, with a postscript tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-headed muscle at the back of the upper arm straightens the elbow.

clue.text: Strict doctor with papers

parts.note: to doctor results is to falsify or rig them
ID, identity documents, are one's papers

explanation.surface: A doctor who demands proper paperwork is a stickler.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflexible and unbending rules are strict, harsh and severe.

clue.text: Plot everything with setter surrounded by books about religion

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: surrounded by means the setter's pronoun sits between the two testament abbreviations

parts.note: OT and NT are the Old and New Testaments, the books of the Bible
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A conspiracy in which the setter is hemmed in by religious tomes.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small rented plot of land in Britain where people grow vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A rented patch of ground for gardening is a plot, here the land sense rather than a scheme.

clue.text: Loathing of treated carbon here?

indicators.note: treated, as in chemically processed, means the letters of 'carbon here' are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone's revulsion at chemically processed carbon in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense hatred or disgust is loathing, as is the noun built from the verb abhor.

clue.text: Made uninvited use of resorts in the elevated Kalahari, perhaps

indicators.note: in puts the resorts inside the upturned desert word
elevated in a down clue means the word is raised, reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Kalahari is an example of a desert, in southern Africa
spas are health resorts

explanation.surface: Tourists wandered uninvited into high-altitude spa resorts in the Kalahari.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the Kalahari as just one example of the needed word; 'elevated' fits a down clue, where the word reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Entering another's land without permission is unauthorised use of it, a fair gloss of the verb.

clue.text: Bury substitute — talented and transposable

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
to change is to substitute one thing for another
able means capable or talented

explanation.surface: A football manager's note: bench the substitute, who is gifted and versatile.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that can swap places with each other are transposable or exchangeable.

clue.text: Tries again to get European train

parts.note: a court rehears a case when it tries it again

explanation.surface: A traveller makes another attempt to catch a European train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway noun but is the verb, to practise.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise a performance before the real thing is to prepare or drill, i.e. train.

clue.text: Bouquet arranged around paper shop

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go round the paper's letter
arranged, as flowers are arranged, means the letters of Bouquet are reordered

parts.note: the i is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A florist arranges a bouquet wrapped in paper for a small shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns BOUQUET into BOUTQUE; 'around' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fashionable retail outlet, often selling clothes, is a type of shop.

clue.text: Unusual foresight is a bonus not to be questioned

definitions.text: a bonus not to be questioned

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of foresight appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A rare gift of foresight is a blessing one should not question.
explanation.walkthrough: From the proverb 'never look a gift horse in the mouth': don't inspect a present for flaws.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a free benefit that should be accepted gratefully without scrutiny.

clue.text: Official document the French sent up

parts.note: a form is a document to be filled in

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means the French article reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: An official French document is mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something formal is officially sanctioned or done according to proper procedure.

clue.text: Collapse of square block

parts.note: a lump is a solid block or chunk

explanation.surface: A square block of masonry gives way.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp fall, as in prices or a sitting posture, is a collapse.

clue.text: Unhealthy looking bird, having lost a wife

indicators.note: having lost means the wife letter is taken out of the bird

parts.note: the swallow is a migratory bird
W is the abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A widower bird looks pale and poorly after losing its mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A sallow complexion is yellowish and pallid, suggesting poor health.

clue.text: Superficial sea foam expert

parts.note: surf is the foaming water of breaking waves
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist on sea spray is dismissed as shallow.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjectival sense means outward only, on the top layer, i.e. superficial.

clue.text: Small pale bird

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
wan means pale and sickly

explanation.surface: A little washed-out bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A large white long-necked waterfowl is a bird.

clue.text: Mobilises right supporters

parts.note: allies are supporters or partners

explanation.surface: A right-wing party musters its backers.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally troops or supporters is to gather and rouse them for action.

clue.text: Revolutionary upmarket housing swindle

indicators.note: revolutionary, turning round, means the concealed letters are read backwards
housing means the word upmarket holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: A radical scheme for posh homes turns out to be a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' gives PMAR inside 'upmarket'; 'Revolutionary' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a ramp is a racket or fraud, especially one involving inflated prices.

clue.text: Gather in the morning on a ship

parts.note: a.m. means before noon, in the morning
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Crew assemble at dawn aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate or collect things together is to gather them in.

clue.text: School has nothing certain to provide tranquillity

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive school, the British state secondary school
nothing is zero, shaped like O
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A school confident of nothing at all aims for calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Calmness and self-possession of mind is tranquillity.
